Three-dimensional rainbow schlieren tomography of a temperature field in gas flows
top_cited_works.abstract: We present quantitative rainbow schlieren deflectometry with tomography for measurements of temperature in three-dimensional gas flows. The schlieren apparatus with a continuously graded spectral filter of known transmissivity was used to create color schlieren images of the test media. These images at multiple viewing angles were used to infer beam deflection angles by the medium. The deflection data were used with a tomographic technique to reconstruct the refractive index and thus the temperature field. The temperature distributions obtained by the rainbow schlieren tomography agreed with those measured by a thermocouple probe. This research demonstrates that tomography can be used with full-field schlieren deflectometry to measure quantitatively temperature in asymmetric gas flows. The technique could be used to obtain related properties such as pressure, density, and gas composition.

recent_works.title: Characteristics and Performance of a Novel Radial Rotating Detonation Engine With an Axial Exhaust Throat
recent_works.abstract: In this study, a novel radial rotating detonation engine (RRDE) is introduced, and its operating characteristics, performance, and exhaust flow field are investigated. The RRDE geometry consists of an axial exhaust throat made possible by a complete turning of the flow, from radial to axial, within the combustor. The placement of the throat also allows optical measurements directly above the exit. Data available for analysis include a) capillary tube attenuated pressure ports in the reactant plenums, combustor channel, and on the center bluff body, b) high-speed fluctuating pressure measurements obtained by PCB piezo-electric probes, c) thrust data acquired using a six-axes load cell, d) high-speed downstream imaging, and e) 100 kHz particle image velocimetry measurements on a radial and a chordal plane of the RRDE exit. Experiments were conducted with methane fuel and an oxygen-enriched air mixture as the oxidizer at varying chamber pressures and testing conditions to characterize performance and exhaust flow field.

recent_works.title: High Area Ratio Convergent Nozzle to Improve Performance of Rotating Detonation Engine
recent_works.abstract: Building upon previous research with rapid to gradual (RTG) nozzles of area ratio (AR) up to 4.0, this work examines an RTG nozzle with AR = 6.0 and how it affects wave stability, flow uniformity, and pressure gain in a rotating detonation engine (RDE). The experimental setup utilizes an RDE with methane and oxygen-enriched air (67% O₂ and 33% N₂ by volume) supplied to the combustor in a counterflow arrangement. Tests are conducted at equivalence ratios of 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 and two different mass flow rates (0.18 and 0.32 kg/s), to enable direct comparisons with the previous study. Internal RDE performance is characterized by using pressure measurements across different axial locations, and high-speed imaging at 100 kHz to visualize the wave behavior in the annulus.

recent_works.title: Analysis of Oblique Shock at RDE Exit Using Tomographically Reconstructed Density Fields
recent_works.abstract: Oblique shock interactions with the nearfield ambient at the exit of a Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) are investigated. The study employs Rainbow Schlieren Deflectometry (RSD) to visualize and quantify optical ray deflections. Then, deflectometric tomography is used to reconstruct local 3D density fields in the exhaust flow. Experiments are performed in a methane-fueled annular RDE with oxygen-enriched air (2/3 O2 and 1/3 N2 by mole) at a mass flow rate of 0.45 kg/s and equivalence ratio, ϕ = 1. High-speed RSD images are acquired at 581.25 kHz and an exposure time of 369 ns to minimize smearing. The RDE operates in a 6.7 kHz single-wave mode, providing approximately 86 images per wave cycle. These images are used to assess flow structures qualitatively and to create time-resolved local 3D density fields for each cycle. RSD images and reconstructed fields enable isolation of the oblique shock wave, the separation between the hot products and the cold ambient air, and a high-density spiral structure originating from shock-boundary interaction. Results provide a quantitative analysis of the inherently non-uniform, transient RDE exit flow and help explain its nearfield behavior.

An Open-Source Solenoid Injector Driver Circuit for Fuel Injection Research
recent_works.abstract: Common rail, high-pressure electronic fuel injection is one of the primary technologies enabling high-efficiency and low emissions in modern diesel engines. Most fuel injectors utilize an actively controlled solenoid valve to actuate a needle that modulates the fuel supply into the combustion chamber. The electrical drive circuit for the injector requires extensive development costs, and thus, most designs are proprietary in nature, making it difficult to perform academic studies of the fuel injection processes. This research presents an injector driver circuit to control one or more solenoid injectors simultaneously for research-based injector development efforts. The electrical circuit was computationally modeled and optimized iteratively, and then, electronic hardware was developed to demonstrate control of a Bosch CRIN3 solenoid diesel injector as proof of concept. In addition, the injector performance was quantified by the fuel rate of injection (ROI) profiles obtained in a test rig utilizing the momentum flux method.
